Thereafter it continues to follow the directions indicated in the figure, going back and forth between the positive part of the $x$ and $y$ axes, moving one unit of distance parallel to an axis in each minute. Which point will the particle reach after exactly 2 hours?

The path starts from the origin O, first goes right along the x-axis to (1,0), then goes upward along x=1 to y=1, then goes left to the y-axis; next it goes upward along the y-axis to y=2, then goes right to x=2, then goes downward along x=2 to the x-axis; then it goes right along the x-axis to x=3, then goes upward along x=3 to y=3, then goes left to the y-axis; afterward it continues extending according to the same square polygonal-line path alternating upward and right/downward. Reasoning: The particle travels 1 unit per minute, so 2 hours corresponds to 120 minutes, that is, path length 120. Group according to the repeating structure in the figure: the kth group goes from (2k-2,0) to (2k,0). In the kth group, first go right 1 unit to (2k-1,0); then go in the upward and left directions along the odd side length 2k-1, with total length 2(2k-1); then go upward 1 unit along the y-axis; then go in the right and downward directions along the even side length 2k, with total length 4k. The total length of the kth group is 1+2(2k-1)+1+4k=8k. The total time to complete the first k groups is 8(1+2+...+k)=4k(k+1), and at this time the position is (2k,0). Let 4k(k+1)=120, giving k(k+1)=30, so k=5. Therefore the position after 120 minutes is (2·5,0)=(10,0).
